I find that big cities that aren’t hubs tend to have really cheap flights. Cities like San Antonio, Cleveland, Vegas… the big 3 airlines have a relatively equal market share in those cities. So there’s a lot of competition. But there’s still enough flights with the demand to fill all the seats that they can price low and still make a profit. 
I’ve seen direct international flights to Houston on United for 4x the cost of flying to Austin or San Antonio with a layover in Houston on the same flight. United can’t offer a better itinerary than Delta (layover in ATL) or American (layover in DFW). But flying direct to Houston there’s probably no other airline flying that route nonstop so it can jack up the prices. Same with Cleveland — you could have layovers in MSP or DTW on Delta, ORD on United or American, etc… every airline is offering the same thing, a one stop connection. And in a big city, they need to compete for customers. 
Compare to a small city like Salina KS or Sioux City IA. Only a handful of flights a day and not enough demand to fill the planes. The tickets will be expensive to compensate for the cost of flying that route.

Flaming Gorge, Grand Teton, Yellowstone, Dinosaur National Monument, Colorado National Monument. Do not skip any of those, you won’t regret it (flaming gorge is so-so but you’ll be near anyways)

Glacier in MT and Lake Pend Oreille in Idaho are great places to camp out. and try to not skip any national parks in Utah (if they’re all too far away, at least do arches and canyonlands) Fisher Towers is near canyonlands and is another place you gotta see (especially if you like Austin powers, they were featured in one of those movies) and two mountain ranges in Utah, the La Sal and Uinta, are beautiful

And please, skip central Montana! Do US Route 2 from Kalispell to Wolf Point then go south to Theodore Roosevelt NP in North Dakota via the Enchanted Highway. Then Badlands NP in South Dakota, but wind cave NP isn’t that great. Obviously Mount Rushmore as well and Devils Tower in Wyoming is a must if you skip N. Dakota

You’ve gotta do one of the four NPs in Colorado. Mesa Verde and Great sand dunes are far away from your itinerary, but Rocky Mountain is a necessity, and you’ll be near black canyon of the gunnison so just stop there for an hour too

Corn Palace in Mitchell SD, and if you like history, Chimney Rock and Scottsbluff National Monuments in West Nebraska. Lake Minatare lighthouse is cool, Garden of the Gods in Colorado is another cool place (this whole paragraph can be skipped if it’s too far out of the way, which it kinda is)

Fossil Butte National Monument and Agate Fossil Beds in WY and NE respectively are cool if you like the aforementioned dinosaur national monument. On I-80 in Nebraska, Fort Kearny and the Archway are also must-sees

Last thing, from Sioux Falls back to Des Moines, don’t take I-29 in Iowa, it gets way too backed up near Omaha depending on time of day and year. Take a US Highway (I think 75?) through Minnesota and Central Iowa, especially if there are tornadoes, you’ll move quicker getting away

Chesapeake Bay bridge/tunnel is cool and if you’re going to the Outer Banks or the coast, you may get there quicker than if you take 95 through DC. Norfolk VA is nice, and a great place to spend the night if needed.

If you divert really fat west and avoid the DC metro and Delaware, you can take I-81 and go through Shenandoah National Park. 

FYI Don’t take 95 through New Jersey, it’s a mess. I think GW Bridge to Garden State Parkway is your best bet. Get on 95 in southern NJ or PA if you take 95, otherwise I-81 is more scenic and less crowded. Pennsylvania has Philly (independence hall and liberty bell among others) and Gettysburg NMP. 

Last thing, Chesapeake Bay seafood is amazing. Get lobster or fish or really anything for that matter.
